description: §14.8.9 — declassification is COLUMN-keyed, not existence-keyed. `passwordHash` is the protected column; the body reveals `email`. That reveal declassifies nothing about `passwordHash`, so the raw-egress gate still fires E-PROTECT-004. The adversarial twin of `reveal-suppresses-e004`, which reveals the RIGHT column and is correctly silent.
rationale: §14.8.9: `reveal("col")` stamps THE NAMED COLUMN's provenance descriptor as declassified-at-this-value — it is a per-column admit, not a per-body switch. Until S405 the gate's suppression tested only for the PRESENCE of a `.reveal(` anywhere in the body, so revealing any column disarmed the gate for every protected column in that body: `reveal("email")` silently declassified `passwordHash`. This case pins the narrowed rule — the gate is discharged only when every protected OUTPUT column of the offending query is named by a reveal. It goes red against the pre-S405 emitter, which is what makes it a proof rather than a description. ⚑ S441 (`g-protected-column-escapes-redaction-as-scalar`): `I-PROTECT-STRIP-001` no longer co-fires here, because nothing is stripped — the info now fires only for a query whose row the egress sink ACTUALLY stripped (the §14.8.9 provenance flow, `compiler/src/codegen/protect-flow.ts`). Before S441 it fired for every protected SELECT, and this case pinned that false claim. `E-PROTECT-006` co-fires on the same column-keyed basis: `reveal("email")` does not declassify `passwordHash`, so the row that crosses into the slice still carries it, and what comes back out of code the flow cannot see into reaches the response outside its row. ⚑ S455 (`g-foreign-iife-captures-module-scope-s454`): a `_={ }=` slice sees ONLY what its `in:{}` header crosses (§23.2.4a). This case's slice used to read `u` without crossing it, which only compiled-and-ran because the old in-place IIFE leaked the enclosing scope; it now crosses what it reads. The reveal moved OUT of the slice with it: `reveal` is scrml, and the opaque slice text is never lowered.
